terminals.name: e2e-stack
terminals.command: make e2e-env-up && .cursor/trust-fake-google.sh && echo 'E2E stack is healthy' && cd e2e/playwright && docker compose --profile fake logs -f --tail 0
terminals.description: Boots the stack from e2e/playwright/docker-compose.yml and then tails its logs: Mattermost at http://localhost:8075, Postgres on 5434, and a fake Google (e2e/playwright/fake-google/server.ts) standing in for Google's OAuth, Calendar and People APIs. Wait for 'E2E stack is healthy'. There is no real Google here. Build and install the plugin with `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_SITEURL=http://localhost:8075 MM_ADMIN_USERNAME=<admin> MM_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<password> make deploy`, then in System Console > Plugins > Google Calendar set OAuth client ID fake-gcal-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com and secret fake-gcal-client-secret and generate an encryption key. accounts.google.com is mapped to the fake in /etc/hosts, so connecting from the browser opens the fake's consent page, which signs in as owner@fake-google.test or collab@fake-google.test. The server starts with no users (the first account created becomes the system admin); the Playwright suite (`make e2e`) creates sysadmin / Sys@dmin-sample1. Reset all data with `make e2e-env-down && make e2e-env-up && .cursor/trust-fake-google.sh`.
